items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Jimmy Blythe groups' and 'Cathedral Blues he's on', but the interviewee (Ernest 'Punch' Miller) does not respond to this specific mention or provide any personal anecdote, connection, or confirmation of meeting Jimmy Blythe.

ctx.x: I thought that record came out on their, under another name, too. Yeah.

Like one of the Jimmy Blythe groups. Yeah, I think maybe it did. Uh, Cathedral Blues he's on, and Dixieland Doings the other side, it's another trouble. We thought maybe it was Frankie Halfbine with the vocal, but he can't hear too well.

Uh, do you know anything about Tiny Parham? I never did get to talk to him. I saw him play once at the Savoy Ballroom in 1938. Yeah. He's a big, big, fat doll was playing the organ. That's right. And I went over there with Mead Lux Lewis, and I said, who's the organist? He said, oh, everybody knows him. If you know him, that's Tiny. Yeah, that's right. A big, big, big fella.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: And Blythe on the piano. Oh I forgot all about that.

ctx.x: Well he's the leader of the band, so it must be his band. It must have been. It's under his name.
It must have been. Well. And Blythe on the piano. Oh I forgot all about that. Yeah.
